newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast spot prods unchanged amid flat trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast spot prods unchanged amid flat trade.

text.p: Spot prices for U.S. West Coast products were flat Friday, amid ample supply and anemic demand as traders left the market early for the weekend, players said.
NYMEX crude oil ftures failed to give West Coast spot trade a lift, easing four cents a barrel to $19.99 after a technical rally fizzled in late trade.
Adequate West Coast gasoline supply soured trader interest in the futures gains, with stocks up 578,000 barrels to 26.7 million barrels last week, according to the American Petroleum Institute.
Los Angeles ultra-clean wholesale gasoline (CARB) was peeged at 70/71 cents a gallon, unchanged from Thursday, with L.A. conventional unleaded at 66/67 cents a gallon
San Francisco gasolines were assessed about 1.50 cents a gallon under L.A.
Distillates in northern and southern California were also seen flat, with low sulphur diesel fuel at 58/59 cents a gallon, and CARB diesel at 70/71 cents.
